Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: grayscale MRI-like educational game image, 1024x1024 square on solid pure black. This is a synthetic teaching illustration, not a quantitative clinical scan. Primary request: one anatomically plausible mid-coronal slice through an ADULT RIGHT WRIST, distal radius and smaller ulna below, two orderly rows of carpal bones across center and proximal metacarpal bases above, enough surrounding soft tissue. Appearance of non-fat-suppressed T1-weighted MRI: fatty marrow in radius, ulna, carpals and metacarpals relatively bright, subcutaneous fat bright, cortical bone and tendons dark, thin joint fluid low signal; muscle intermediate-to-low gray. Distal radius at screen left, ulnar head at screen right, coherent carpal rows, no extra bones or fingers. Adult closed growth plates. Natural realistic grayscale MR texture and modest acquisition grain, not an X-ray and not a cartoon/pixel scene. Neutral mild soft-tissue clinical question only, do not invent dramatic fracture, tumor, bone loss, screws or surgical implants. Centered anatomy filling about 80 percent height, with black margin. One slice only, no montage, no orientation letters, no measurements, no text, no markers or arrows, no watermark. This image will be the exact geometric reference for a matching T2 image, so anatomy must be clean and stable.

Use case: precise-object-edit / scientific-educational. EDIT THE SUPPLIED WRIST MRI TEACHING IMAGE. Preserve exact anatomy, every bone outline, carpal arrangement, crop, orientation, pose, soft-tissue contour and all coordinates. Change ONLY tissue-specific MRI contrast from the T1-like reference into a plausible matching conventional NON-fat-suppressed T2-weighted appearance. Joint fluid and small normal recesses become bright relative to T1; fat remains relatively bright but less dominant, fatty bone marrow moderately bright, muscle stays intermediate-low, tendons/ligaments/cortex remain dark. This must not be a global brightness change: fluid gets brighter and fat-versus-water contrast changes independently. No new fracture, edema, mass, fluid collection or lesion; no new anatomical structures. Keep same modest grain and black background, same square image. No labels, no arrow, no text, no UI. The two images are nonquantitative matching synthetic teaching illustrations, not real patient data.
